definition.text: Human anatomy and physiology organizes body structure from chemical components to cells, tissues, organs, organ systems, and the organism, so students can connect form to function across scales.

anchor.quote: Life processes of the human body are maintained at several levels of structural organization

facts.text: A cell is the smallest independently functioning unit of a living organism.

anchor.quote: A cell is the smallest independently functioning unit of a living organism

facts.text: Organs are anatomically distinct structures made of two or more tissue types.

anchor.quote: An organ is an anatomically distinct structure of the body composed of two or more tissue types

misconceptions.text: Students may memorize structures as isolated labels.
misconceptions.corrective: Labels matter, but the A&P backbone is structure-function reasoning across levels of organization.

definition.text: Homeostasis is the maintenance of stable internal conditions, usually through negative-feedback loops that detect a deviation from a set point and activate a response that reverses it.

anchor.quote: Negative feedback is a mechanism that reverses a deviation from the set point

facts.text: A set point is the physiological value around which the normal range fluctuates.

anchor.quote: A set point is the physiological value around which the normal range fluctuates

facts.text: A feedback loop includes a sensor, a control center, and an effector.

anchor.quote: An effector is the component in a feedback system that causes a change to reverse the situation and return the value to the normal range

misconceptions.text: Students may read negative feedback as a harmful response.
misconceptions.corrective: Negative describes the direction of correction: the response opposes the deviation from the set point.

definition.text: The four broad tissue categories are epithelial, connective, muscle, and nervous tissue, each with structures and functions that support body organization.

anchor.quote: they are organized into four broad categories of tissues: epithelial, connective, muscle, and nervous

facts.text: Histology studies tissue appearance, organization, and function under the microscope.

anchor.quote: histology, the microscopic study of tissue appearance, organization, and function

facts.text: Tissue cells share morphological features and an orderly arrangement that supports tissue function.

anchor.quote: share morphological features and are arranged in an orderly pattern that achieves the tissue's functions

misconceptions.text: Students may treat tissue identification as matching colors only.
misconceptions.corrective: Identification should connect microscopic organization to the tissue's function and location.

definition.text: Epithelial tissue forms sheets of cells that cover body surfaces, line cavities and passageways, and form glands.

anchor.quote: refers to the sheets of cells that cover exterior surfaces of the body, line internal cavities and passageways, and form certain glands

facts.text: Epithelial tissue is one of the four primary tissue categories.

anchor.quote: epithelial, connective, muscle, and nervous

misconceptions.text: Students may assume epithelial tissue is only skin.
misconceptions.corrective: Epithelium also lines internal cavities and passageways and forms glands.

definition.text: Connective tissue binds cells and organs together and supports protection, support, and integration across body parts.

anchor.quote: binds the cells and organs of the body together and functions in the protection, support, and integration

facts.text: Connective tissue is one of the four primary tissue categories.

anchor.quote: epithelial, connective, muscle, and nervous

misconceptions.text: Students may assume connective tissue has one uniform appearance.
misconceptions.corrective: Connective tissues vary widely because their roles include support, protection, binding, and integration.

definition.text: The integumentary system includes the skin and accessory structures; skin has epidermal and dermal layers that support protection and communication.

anchor.quote: The skin and its accessory structures make up the integumentary system

facts.text: The skin has two main layers: the epidermis and dermis.

anchor.quote: The skin is composed of two main layers: the epidermis

facts.text: The epidermis is made of keratinized stratified squamous epithelium.

anchor.quote: The epidermis is composed of keratinized, stratified squamous epithelium

misconceptions.text: Students may treat skin as a simple covering.
misconceptions.corrective: Skin is an organ system surface with layered tissues, sensory structures, vessels, glands, and protective functions.

definition.text: The skeletal system is made of bones and cartilage and supports the body, enables movement, protects organs, produces blood cells, and stores minerals and fat.

anchor.quote: supports the body, facilitates movement, protects internal organs, produces blood cells, stores and releases minerals and fat

facts.text: Bone is hard, dense connective tissue that forms most of the adult skeleton.

anchor.quote: Bone, or osseous tissue, is a hard, dense connective tissue

facts.text: Bones facilitate movement by providing attachment points for muscles.

anchor.quote: Bones also facilitate movement by serving as points of attachment for your muscles

misconceptions.text: Students may view bones as passive supports only.
misconceptions.corrective: Bones support, protect, store minerals and fat, produce blood cells, and act with muscles and joints to produce movement.

definition.text: Synovial joints are common movable joints with a joint cavity, articular cartilage, synovial fluid, and supporting ligaments that allow smooth motion.

anchor.quote: Synovial joints allow for smooth movements between the adjacent bones

facts.text: A key structural feature of a synovial joint is a fluid-filled joint cavity.

anchor.quote: A key structural characteristic for a synovial joint that is not seen at fibrous or cartilaginous joints is the presence of a joint cavity

facts.text: Ligaments support synovial joints by holding bones together and resisting abnormal motion.

anchor.quote: Ligaments support the joint by holding the bones together and resisting excess or abnormal joint motions

misconceptions.text: Students may treat every joint as structurally identical.
misconceptions.corrective: Synovial joints have a joint cavity and specialized structures that explain their mobility.

definition.text: Muscle tissue includes skeletal, cardiac, and smooth muscle; all are excitable, and contractility lets muscle pull on attachment points and shorten with force.

anchor.quote: the body contains three types of muscle tissue: skeletal muscle, cardiac muscle, and smooth muscle

facts.text: All three muscle tissue types share excitability.

anchor.quote: they all exhibit a quality called excitability

facts.text: Skeletal muscle depends on nervous-system signaling to work properly.

anchor.quote: skeletal muscle completely depends on signaling from the nervous system to work properly

misconceptions.text: Students may assume all muscle is voluntary skeletal muscle.
misconceptions.corrective: Cardiac and smooth muscle differ from skeletal muscle in control, location, structure, and physiological regulation.

definition.text: Nervous tissue is excitable tissue made mainly of neurons and neuroglia; neurons propagate information through electrochemical impulses called action potentials.

anchor.quote: Two main classes of cells make up nervous tissue: the neuron and neuroglia

facts.text: Nervous tissue sends and receives electrochemical signals that provide the body with information.

anchor.quote: capable of sending and receiving electrochemical signals that provide the body with information

facts.text: Neuroglia support neurons and modulate information propagation.

anchor.quote: Neuroglia play an essential role in supporting neurons and modulating their information propagation

misconceptions.text: Students may treat glial cells as unimportant filler.
misconceptions.corrective: Neuroglia are essential support and modulation cells for nervous-system function.

definition.text: Sensory receptors detect internal or external stimuli and convert them into nervous-system signals; perception is the central processing of those signals into meaningful patterns.

anchor.quote: Perception is the central processing of sensory stimuli into a meaningful pattern

facts.text: Receptors are cells or structures that detect sensations.

anchor.quote: Receptors are the cells or structures that detect sensations

facts.text: Stimuli are changed into electrochemical signals of the nervous system.

anchor.quote: Stimuli from varying sources, and of different types, are received and changed into the electrochemical signals of the nervous system

misconceptions.text: Students may use sensation and perception as interchangeable terms.
misconceptions.corrective: Sensation is receptor activation; perception is central processing into a meaningful pattern.

definition.text: Hormones circulate through the bloodstream but affect only target cells with the appropriate receptors, triggering target-cell responses that regulate physiological processes.

anchor.quote: it will affect the activity only of its target cells; that is, cells with receptors for that particular hormone

facts.text: Hormone binding initiates a chain of events that leads to a target-cell response.

anchor.quote: Once the hormone binds to the receptor, a chain of events is initiated that leads to the target cell's response

facts.text: Hormones regulate processes including growth, metabolism, fluid balance, electrolyte balance, and sleep.

anchor.quote: metabolism, fluid, and electrolyte balance, sleep, and many other body functions

misconceptions.text: Students may assume every circulating hormone acts on every cell.
misconceptions.corrective: Only target cells with the right receptors respond to a given hormone.
